findings.message: checkout without persist-credentials: false — tokens may leak
findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: Checkout without persist-credentials: false leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for any process to read.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout defaults to persist-credentials: true — token leaks via .git/config.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: declares a prepare lifecycle script
findings.remediation: Remove install-time side effects or document and review each lifecycle script.
findings.impact: Install-time lifecycle scripts execute with full npm privileges — preinstall RCE is a classic attack.
findings.attack_vector: package.json scripts.preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare — runs arbitrary code during npm install.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains 3 line(s) longer than 500 characters (possible minified/obfuscated code)
findings.remediation: Review extremely long lines; they may contain hidden logic.
findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.
findings.attack_vector: Lines > 500 chars — code is structured to evade visual inspection.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads a likely secret source and opens a network connection in the same source file
findings.remediation: Keep secrets out of agent-visible output and require an allowlisted destination before egress.
findings.impact: Secret source + network sink in same file = direct exfiltration pathway for credentials.
findings.attack_vector: File reads secrets (process.env/credential files) AND opens network connections — data flows out.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.attack_vector: File path matches ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, or ~/.docker/config.json.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
